items.stem:
Priya walks from her home to a park, waits there, and then walks straight home again.
The travel graph shows her journey.

parts.t: Write down how long Priya waits at the park.

Work out her walking speed for the first 30 minutes.
Give your answer in km/h.

sols: While Priya waits, her distance from home does not change, so the graph is horizontal.
The horizontal section runs from 30 minutes to 50 minutes.
In the first 30 minutes she walks 3 km.
read the first vertex off the graph
the answer is asked for in km/h, so the time must be in hours

accept read from the intersection of the two lines

the line slopes downwards because the distance from X is decreasing

A1
accept 15 km from home stated

At t = 1 Mia is also 15 km from home, since her rest lasts from 10:45 to 11:00.
read the end of the horizontal section

Amira sets off on a hike at 08:00.
The travel graph shows her distance from the start during the morning. Her walk has four stages.

parts.t: Between which two times does Amira walk fastest? Give a reason for your answer.
Write down the time at which she is 6 km from the start.

ms:
B1 for 09:00 to 10:30 (or “the second stage”)
B1 for “steepest gradient” oe, e.g. 6 km in 1.5 h = 4 km/h is the largest speed
sols: Speed is the gradient of a distance–time graph, so the fastest stage is the steepest line.
The stages have speeds 3 ÷ 1 = 3 km/h, 6 ÷ 1.5 = 4 km/h, 1 ÷ 0.5 = 2 km/h and 2 ÷ 1 = 2 km/h.
distance covered divided by time taken for each stage
She walks fastest between 09:00 and 10:30, because that section of the graph is the steepest.
Read across from 6 on the distance axis to the graph, then down to the time axis.
6 km is reached during the second stage, at 3 + 4 × 0.75 = 6, i.e. 45 minutes after 09:00.

Villages A and B are 10 km apart.
Ana leaves A at 08:00 and walks to B, resting once on the way.
Ben leaves B at 08:45 and cycles to A along the same road at a constant speed of 12 km/h.
The travel graph shows both journeys.

parts.t: Calculate Ana's speed on the last stage of her walk.
Find the time at which Ben passes Ana.
Find the time at which Ben arrives at A.
How far apart are Ana and Ben at 09:30?

sols: Ana's last stage runs from (09:30, 4) to (11:00, 10): 6 km in 1.5 h.
Ana rests at 4 km from 09:00 to 09:30.
Ben must cover 10 − 4 = 6 km to reach her: 6 ÷ 12 = 0.5 h = 30 minutes.
08:45 + 30 min = 09:15, which is during Ana's rest, so this is when they meet.
the lines cross on the horizontal part of Ana's graph
Ben covers 10 km at 12 km/h: 10 ÷ 12 = <sup>5</sup>⁄<sub>6</sub> h = 50 minutes.
At 09:30 Ana is still at 4 km. Ben has cycled 45 min = 0.75 h: 12 × 0.75 = 9 km, so he is 10 − 9 = 1 km from A.

Leo drives from his home to a town 60 km away, stays there for a while, and then drives straight home.

parts.t: Calculate his speed on the way to the town.

A1

Towns P and Q are 150 km apart.
A truck leaves P at 07:00 and drives at a constant speed to Q, arriving at 09:30.
A car leaves P at 07:40 and drives along the same road to Q at a constant speed of 90 km/h.
The travel graph shows both journeys.

parts.t: Calculate the speed of the truck.
Find the time at which the car overtakes the truck, and the distance from P at which this happens.
How far is the truck from Q when the car arrives at Q?

ms:
B1 for 09:00
B1 for 120 km
or M1 for 60t = 90(t − 2⁄3) oe, A1

M1 for car time 150 ÷ 90 = 12⁄3 h (arrives 09:20) or truck at 140 km
A1
cao
sols: The truck covers 150 km between 07:00 and 09:30, i.e. in 2.5 hours.
Let t be the time in hours after 07:00. Truck: 60t. Car: 90(t − 2⁄3).
the car starts 40 minutes = <sup>2</sup>⁄<sub>3</sub> h later
The car overtakes at 09:00, 120 km from P
60 × 2 = 120, matching the crossing point of the two lines
Car time = 150 ÷ 90 = 1<sup>2</sup>⁄<sub>3</sub> h = 1 h 40 min, so it arrives at 09:20.
At 09:20 the truck has driven for 2<sup>1</sup>⁄<sub>3</sub> h: 60 × 2<sup>1</sup>⁄<sub>3</sub> = 140 km.
